_comment: Single source of truth for the ngit release matrix and its shard plan.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
One `act` invocation -- one workflow file -- is bounded by the coordinator's
NGIT_CI_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECS (1800 s on this deployment). The full 14 .ipk + 3 .apk
matrix does not fit that, and neither does any per-arch grouping of it. So
stage 2 is sharded into one workflow file per group of legs whose MEASURED
cost leaves headroom under the ceiling, and this file is where the matrix and
the shard assignment live.
MEASURED COST OF THE EXPENSIVE LEGS (2 CPUs, the per-job cgroup cap)
`upx --ultra-brute` is what made the unsharded run impossible. Two figures,
and the difference between them is the whole argument for sharding:
* ~29 min per leg inside the UNsharded run (2026-09-12, commit b25d8a28),
where 14 package containers shared a 4-vCPU host through a 2-CPU-per-job
cap -- the leg was starved, not slow;
* 515 s (~8.6 min) for the same leg in isolation, measured 2026-09-20 on the
aarch64_cortex-a53 pair (11.5 MB + 6.7 MB binaries) under `taskset -c 0,1`
with the pinned upx 5.2.1. --fast 1.5 s, --best 67 s, --brute 401 s.
So a shard that holds ONE ultra-brute leg costs under ten minutes and fits
with room to spare; a shard that holds five of them does not. Do not read the
515 s as licence to stack legs: the coordinator's host is shared, the CI job
also pays the Blossom downloads, and a timed-out shard is what this plan
exists to prevent. Re-measure before merging two legs into one shard.
Also note: the workflow installs `upx-ucl` from apt, which is NOT the pinned
upx 5.2.1 from packaging/build-inputs.json. The measurements above use the
pinned binary. Pinning the CI one is a separate change.
Stage 1 (.ngit/act/workflows/build-package-binaries.yml) is unchanged and is
still located through the kind-30078 handover records.
GENERATED FROM THIS FILE
scripts/ngit-gen-shards.py renders .ngit/act/workflows/build-package-<id>.yml
from the `shards` below. The rendered files are committed (act needs static
YAML) and `scripts/ngit-gen-shards.py --check` fails when they drift.
READ BY
scripts/ngit-shards.sh        plan queries (legs, shard ids, expectations)
scripts/ngit-release-announce.sh  completeness gate before anything is announced
scripts/verify_publication.sh expectations (via scripts/ngit-shards.sh)
scripts/ngit-ci-release.sh    the ordered trigger driver
budget_secs is the shard's budget: the measured wall time where a run has been
measured (see `measured_secs`), otherwise the estimate that set the shard's
grain. It must stay under 1500 s so that the 1800 s ceiling keeps a real margin.

shards.note: Every compression=none .ipk leg. Measured 2026-09-12 (inside the unsharded 1800 s run) at under 7 minutes for five legs; this shard is the whole none set.
The two cheap UPX levels, measured on the 2-CPU cap against aarch64_cortex-a53: --fast 1.5 s, --best 67 s. Cheap enough to share one shard.
One leg per shard from here on: --brute and --ultra-brute are minutes of pure single-threaded CPU each and cannot be stacked inside one 1800 s invocation.

The SDK leg: pull openwrt/sdk:<target>@<pinned digest>, run it as a container against the dind sidecar, package and stream the .apk out. It needs a whole invocation to itself -- on the unsharded run its container was created and then never got a slot while 14 .ipk jobs held the host.
